title: A supported Koszul test controls high truncation of open localization
statement:
Work in the universes of [def-weil-size-convention]. Let $S$ be a scheme [def-pc-scheme] and $X$ a quasi-compact quasi-separated algebraic space over $S$ [def-trf-algebraic-space]: every open cover of $|X|$ has a finite subcover, and the absolute diagonal is quasi-compact. Use its small etale structure sheaf $\mathcal O_X$, module sheaves [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category], and unbounded derived category $D(\mathcal O_X)$ [def-weil-abstract-derived-category]. Let $C_X=D_{\mathrm{QCoh}}(\mathcal O_X)$ be the full subcategory with quasi-coherent cohomology [def-trf-space-quasi-coherent-module]. Perfect means etale locally represented by a bounded complex of direct summands of finite free structure modules [def-weil-pbc-strict-perfect-coefficient-package]. Let $(i:U\hookrightarrow X,p:V\to X)$ be an elementary distinguished square: $U$ is a quasi-compact open subspace [def-a1-space-open-subspace], $p$ is representable etale, $V=\operatorname{Spec}A$ is affine, and $V\times_X Z\to Z$ is an isomorphism for the reduced closed subspace $Z$ of $X$ with underlying set $|X|\setminus|U|$ [lem-sfb-space-reduced-closed-support]. Put $T=U\times_XV$. There is a finite list $f_1,\ldots,f_r\in A$ with $T=\bigcup_{k=1}^rD(f_k)$. For every such list, let $B\in D(\mathcal O_V)$ be the associated etale complex of the Koszul complex $K_\bullet(f_1,\ldots,f_r)$ [def-weil-pbc-koszul-complex], placed in cohomological degrees $-r,\ldots,0$ by $B^{-n}=\widetilde {K_n}$ [lem-sfb-affine-etale-derived-module-realization]. Use canonical derived module functors [lem-sfb-space-derived-etale-chart-calculus] and standard truncation [def-sbc-standard-tstructure-derived-category]. Then $B_X=Rp_*B$ is perfect. For every $E\in C_X$, if $\operatorname{Hom}_{D(\mathcal O_X)}(B_X,E[j])=0$ for all sufficiently positive integers $j$, there exists $a\in\mathbf Z$ such that the canonical open-adjunction unit induces an isomorphism in $D(\mathcal O_X)$
$$\tau_{\ge a}E\xrightarrow{\sim}\tau_{\ge a}Ri_*(i^*E).$$

source.place: Tag 0GFH, proposition-detecting-bounded-above, distinguished-square proof from the construction of K and K' through the canonical high-truncation comparison; supported transport: Tags 08HK lemma-pushforward-perfect and 08GG lemma-pushforward-with-support-in-open; affine orthogonality: perfect.tex Tag 0GEJ lemma-orthogonal-koszul-first-variant.

proof.text: The open $U$ is quasi-separated: its absolute diagonal is the base change of the absolute diagonal of $X$ along $U\times U\to X\times X$. The affine scheme $V$ is qcqs. Apply the qcqs fibre-product lemma to $U\to X\leftarrow V$; its three spaces are qcqs, so $T$ is quasi-compact. The principal opens form a basis on $V=\operatorname{Spec}A$. Refine $T$ by this basis and take a finite subcover, giving the list in the statement. When $T=\varnothing$ the empty list is allowed.

source.place: Tag 0GFH, proposition-detecting-bounded-above, paragraph Say V = Spec(A); finite principal-open cover.

proof.text: Fix any such list. The Koszul definition gives $K_q$ the finite basis of increasing $q$-element subsets, with zero terms for $q>r$. Exact affine etale realization sends $A$ and its finite direct sums to $\mathcal O_V$ and its finite direct sums. Thus $B^{-q}=\widetilde K_q$ is an actual bounded finite free representative, making $B$ perfect. On $D(f_k)$ put $h(x)=f_k^{-1}e_k\wedge x$. The displayed Koszul differential satisfies $d(e_k\wedge x)=f_kx-e_k\wedge dx$, so $dh+hd=\mathrm{id}$. This gives a contraction after sheafification, also on every etale object over $D(f_k)$. Hence $B|_T=0$. For $r=0$ the assertion about this restriction is vacuous, and $B=\mathcal O_V[0]$.

source.place: Tag 0GFH, Koszul construction; more-algebra.tex Tags 0622 and 0623, differential and exterior bases.

proof.text: Apply supported etale excision to $F=B$, using $B|_T=0$. It gives $p^*B_X\cong B$, $i^*B_X=0$, and the natural bijections $\operatorname{Hom}(B_X,E[j])\cong\operatorname{Hom}(B,p^*E[j])$. The family $U\amalg V\to X$ is a surjective etale cover: $U$ covers its own points and $V$ covers the complement because it is an isomorphism over $Z$. To check perfectness using the strict-perfect definition, choose a representative $L^\bullet$ of $B_X$. On the part over $U$ it is acyclic and $0\to L^\bullet|_U$ is a quasi-isomorphism. On the part over $V$ the isomorphism from the bounded finite free representative of $B$ to $L^\bullet|_V$ is, locally, an actual chain map by the strict-perfect local-actual lemma. Such a map is a quasi-isomorphism, since its image in the derived category is invertible. Pull back this covering to each etale object of $X$. It exhibits the local representatives required by the definition, proving that $B_X$ is perfect. The Hom bijections transfer the assumed positive-degree vanishing to $B$ on $V$.

source.place: Tags 08GG lemma-pushforward-with-support-in-open and 08HK lemma-pushforward-perfect; Tag 0GFH, K prime and Hom formula; sites-cohomology.tex Tag 08FR lemma-local-actual (1).

proof.text: Let $E_V=p^*E$. It has quasi-coherent cohomology by the etale chart calculus. Choose $a\in\mathbf Z$ so that $\operatorname{Hom}(B,E_V[n])=0$ for every $n\ge a$. Shifting the source identifies this group with $\operatorname{Hom}(B[-n],E_V)$, so there is no reversal of the bound. Write $k:T\hookrightarrow V$. Use the derived etale/Zariski equivalence on the schemes $V$ and $T$ to represent $E_V$ by $E_0\in D_{\mathrm{QCoh}}(\mathcal O_{V,\mathrm{Zar}})$. The associated Koszul object corresponds to the Zariski object $C_f$: affine etale realization is Zariski tilde followed by exact etale pullback. Full faithfulness transfers the Hom vanishing. The affine upper-localization lemma therefore gives $\tau_{\ge a}E_0\to\tau_{\ge a}Rk_{\mathrm{Zar},*}(E_0|_T)$ invertible. The topology comparison is exact, hence commutes with standard truncations. Its direct-image comparison applies: $T$ is a quasi-compact open of the affine scheme $V$, so $k$ is quasi-compact and separated. The canonical pullback and direct-image comparisons identify the units, since their transposes are the identity of the restricted object. Transporting this very map gives the canonical isomorphism $\tau_{\ge a}E_V\to\tau_{\ge a}Rk_*(E_V|_T)$.

source.place: Tag 0GFH, application of perfect.tex Tag 0GEJ lemma-orthogonal-koszul-first-variant; Tags 08H8, 071Q and 08GH for the comparison of topologies.

proof.text: Let $u:E\to Ri_*i^*E$ be the specified unit. Etale base change in the chart calculus, with its unit compatibility, identifies $p^*u$ with $E_V\to Rk_*(E_V|_T)$. Over $U$ the same calculation is base change along the open immersion itself, so $i^*u$ is the identity of $i^*E$. Exact restriction commutes with kernels, cokernels and cohomology, hence with standard truncation. Thus $\tau_{\ge a}u$ restricts to isomorphisms on $V$ by step 4 and on $U$ by the identity calculation. Its cone has zero cohomology after restriction to both members of the cover $U\amalg V\to X$. For each etale object, sections of any of these cohomology sheaves vanish on the pulled-back cover and therefore vanish by the sheaf axiom. The cone is consequently acyclic. In the derived category, the localization at quasi-isomorphisms, this makes $\tau_{\ge a}u$ invertible. This proves the asserted derived isomorphism for the canonical map itself.

source.place: Tag 0GFH, check that the canonical map is an isomorphism after restricting to U and to V.
